subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following correctly describes the shape, orientation and sand-supply condition of a barchan dune?
options: Crescent-shaped, horns downwind. In areas of limited sand supply
Star dune with multiple arms radiating outward from a central peak
Long straight ridge of sand aligned parallel to the prevailing wind
Crescent-shaped dune with its two horns pointing directly upwind
solution: Barchan: single direction wind. Moves by sand avalanching on slip face.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Liquid immiscibility in magmas produces two coexisting melts; in the Skaergaard and Palisades examples, these two melts are:
options: Fe-rich (ferrobasalt) + Si-rich (rhyolite). Immiscible globules. Skaergaard, Palisades
Partial melting of the source rock leaving a restite of olivine and pyroxene
Fractional crystallization of olivine and plagioclase from a basaltic parent magma in the chamber
Assimilation of silica-rich country rock into the ascending magma
solution: Liquid immiscibility: Fe-Ti-P enrichment. Carbonatite-silicate immiscibility also.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 8% moisture, 30% volatile matter and 20% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (8+30+20) = 42%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The full spreading rate at a mid-ocean ridge, used to measure seafloor creation, is defined as what quantity?
options: Speed at which magnetic anomalies move away from the ridge axis
Rate of creation of new oceanic crust measured on only one flank
Velocity of the hotspot relative to the overriding plate motion
Rate of separation of two plates at ridge
solution: Full rate: total separation velocity. Half rate: half. Slow: <5cm/yr. Fast: >8cm/yr. Ultrafast: >15cm/yr.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A linear hotspot track of volcanoes records what about the plate moving over it?
options: Plate motion over stationary mantle plume
Temporal sequence of historical volcanic eruptions
Distribution of earthquake epicenters along a fault
Direction of prevailing ocean surface currents
solution: Hotspot: deep mantle plume. Age-progressive volcanic chain.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In foraminifera biostratigraphy, planktonic forms are used for Mesozoic-Cenozoic zonation, while benthic forms are used for what?
options: Only benthic foraminifera. Zonation is confined to shelf carbonates of the Cenozoic, with planktonic forms ignored
Only radiolarian tests. Their siliceous skeletons define zones in platform carbonates
Planktonic (globigerinids) for Mesozoic-Cenozoic. Benthic for paleobathymetry. δ¹⁸O in tests
Only ostracod carapaces. Chitinous hinges provide the stratigraphic control in deep strata
solution: Forams: CaCO₃ tests. Planktonic: index fossils for Cretaceous-Tertiary. Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Oxygenation event ~2.4 Ga (GOE) caused by:
options: Cyanobacteria photosynthesis
Widespread subaerial volcanic outgassing of oxygen
Continuous asteroid impacts releasing trapped oxygen
Methane oxidation in the primitive reducing atmosphere
solution: GOE: Great Oxidation Event. Cyanobacteria produced O2. Banded iron formations ended. Mass extinction of anaerobes.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Rare earth element deposits often associated with:
options: Alkaline igneous rocks and carbonatites
Quartzose sandstone formations deposited in fluvial braided systems
Thick platform limestone sequences of shallow-marine origin
Black organic-rich shale deposited in anoxic barred basins
solution: REE: concentrated in alkaline complexes, carbonatites.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Fission track dating is a geochronological method that relies on counting which features preserved in minerals?
options: Damage trails from uranium fission
Random structural defects in the crystal lattice
The boundaries between adjacent mineral grains
Cleavage planes developed during mineral breakage
solution: Fission tracks: 238U spontaneous fission creates damage. Etched and counted. Annealing temperature determines closure.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Granulite is a high-grade metamorphic rock distinguished by the presence of which mineral assemblage?
options: High-grade metamorphic. No hydrous minerals (pyroxene + feldspar + garnet)
Low-grade metamorphic rock rich in chlorite, muscovite, biotite and quartz minerals
Contact metamorphic hornfels formed adjacent to a large igneous intrusion
Mica-rich rock with a strong foliation formed at low to medium grade
solution: Granulite: dry metamorphism. H2O absent. Pyroxene stable, biotite unstable.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Reaction rim (coronite) texture indicates:
options: Chemical disequilibrium between minerals
Slow equilibrium crystallization from a melt
Rapid quenching of a high-temperature lava
Mechanical mixing during sedimentary transport
solution: Coronite: rim of new minerals between reacting minerals. Indicates P-T conditions changed, minerals reacting.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What are the characteristic Quaternary deposits and settings found in different regions of India?
options: Marine carbonate platform deposited in a warm shallow tropical sea in the Himalaya
Volcanic basalt flows covering most of the peninsular Indian shield region
Glacial deposits only, restricted to the higher reaches of the Aravalli range
Karewa (Kashmir, glacial), laterite (peninsular, tropical), alluvium (Indus-Ganga)
solution: Karewa: Pleistocene lake deposits. Loess in Kashmir. Sea level changes.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Karst topography characteristically develops in which type of rock?
options: Soluble rocks (limestone, dolomite)
Quartz-rich sandstone with silica cement
Impermeable shale under humid conditions
Porphyritic basalt with columnar jointing
solution: Karst: dissolution of soluble rock. Features: sinkholes, caves, disappearing streams, dolines, poljes.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following is a suitable foundation type on rock?
options: Only wooden piles driven to refusal at the weathered rock surface below the overburden soil
Only shallow footings placed directly on heavily weathered rock at the surface
No foundation of any kind is required when rock is exposed at the surface
Spread footing, raft, pile (socketed into rock). Rock socket friction + end bearing
solution: Socketed piles: shear resistance along rock socket. Roughness increases capacity.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Pressure solution cleavage in deformed rocks develops chiefly by which mechanism of strain accommodation?
options: Fracture cleavage formed by closely spaced brittle fractures confined to competent sandstone and limestone beds
Strain accommodation by dissolution (Stylolite, dissolution seams). Insoluble residue (clay, organics, pyrite)
Mica alignment produced by rotation and growth of phyllosilicate minerals
Slaty cleavage developed perpendicular to the maximum compression direction
solution: Pressure solution: σ₁ perpendicular / σ₃ parallel. Pressure shadow: fibers in low-stress zones.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following correctly describes an arroyo and the environment in which it develops?
options: Steep-walled, flat-floored ephemeral channel in arid regions. Incised
Channel that carries flowing water continuously throughout the entire year without drying
Broad valley with steep walls and a flat floor carved by glacial ice
Multiple unstable channels that split and rejoin around mid-channel bars
solution: Arroyo: incision by base level fall or climate change. SW USA. Valley fill.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Magma mixing of two batches produces which disequilibrium textures in minerals such as plagioclase and augite?
options: Fractionation of early-formed crystals like olivine and pyroxene to produce progressively more felsic residual melts
Mixing of two magma batches. Disequilibrium textures: sieve (plagioclase), reverse zoning (augite overgrowth)
Partial melting of the mantle source at varying degrees of decompression
Assimilation of roof rocks accompanied by convective stirring of the chamber
solution: Mixing: banded pumice, heterogeneous phenocrysts. Mixing + fractional crystallization (MFC).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquifer has hydraulic conductivity 20 m/day and a hydraulic gradient of 0.05. The Darcy velocity is:
options: 20 m/day
400 m/day
2 m/day
1 m/day

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Crystallographic point groups, based on combinations of symmetry elements, number how many in total?
options: 32 crystallographic point groups. m (mirror), 2, 3, 4, 6 (rotation axes), 1 (inversion), 2₁ (screw), etc.
14 groups. The combination of m (mirror), 2, 3, 4, 6 (rotation axes), 1 (inversion) and 2₁ (screw) yields the fourteen Bravais lattices
230 groups. Point group symmetry is completely described by the space group number alone
7 groups. Each point group corresponds to one of the seven crystal systems
solution: Hermann-Mauguin: n (rotation), n̄ (rotoinversion), n/m (mirror ⊥ axis), mm (mirror ∥ axis).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Around rigid porphyroclasts, fibers in pressure shadows grow in which direction relative to the principal stresses?
options: Fibers grow perpendicular to the extension direction in high-pressure zones adjacent to clasts
Fibers precipitate randomly with no preferred orientation around the rigid porphyroclasts
Fibers grow in extension direction (σ₃) in low-pressure zones around rigid porphyroclasts
Fiber growth is controlled by the maximum compressive stress and is parallel to σ₁
solution: Pressure shadows: fibers of quartz, calcite grow in extension direction. Syntaxial vs antitaxial growth.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Seismic discontinuities: Conrad discontinuity:
options: Surface. The discontinuity between the atmosphere and the top of the bedrock
Crust-mantle. It marks the base of the crust and the top of the peridotite mantle
Core-mantle. A worldwide boundary where S-waves are completely stopped
Within continental crust (upper/lower crust boundary)
solution: Conrad: mid-crustal. Vp jump. Not everywhere. Some continents: no Conrad.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The plagioclase feldspar solid-solution series extends between which two end members?
options: Albite (Na) to Anorthite (Ca)
Sanidine to Microcline potassium end members
Albite (Na) to Orthoclase (K) end members
Anorthite (Ca) to Orthoclase (K) end members
solution: Plagioclase: NaAlSi3O8 to CaAl2Si2O8.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Rb-Sr dating, based on ⁸⁷Rb→⁸⁷Sr decay, uses a whole-rock isochron to determine both the age and the initial ⁸⁷Sr/⁸⁶Sr ratio:
options: K-Ar method applied to potassium silicate minerals of the same rock sample being dated
C-14 method on organic remains younger than fifty thousand years old in the strata
⁸⁷Rb → ⁸⁷Sr (β⁻). T½ = 48.8 Ga. Whole-rock isochron. Initial ⁸⁷Sr/⁸⁶Sr ratio
U-Pb method on zircon, monazite and titanite crystals of the rock body being examined
solution: Rb-Sr: isochron method. Initial ratio for magma source (mantle 0.703, crust 0.710).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which statement about basalt as a construction material is correct?
options: Very weak rock that is unsuitable for any construction purpose
Strong, dense. Good aggregate. Columnar joints weaken rock mass
Easily weathered soluble rock with rapid loss of strength
Highly porous rock that absorbs water and disintegrates quickly
solution: Basalt: high UCS (200-350 MPa). Columnar joints → blocky excavation. Used for roads, concrete.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A reverse (or thrust) fault is produced mainly by:
options: Tensional stress
Compressional stress
Hydrostatic pressure
Erosion
solution: Compression pushes the hanging wall up over the footwall — a reverse/thrust fault.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The geoid, an equipotential surface of gravity, deviates from the reference ellipsoid by about how much, and what do its anomalies reflect?
options: Varies ±100m from ellipsoid. Anomalies from density variations in mantle
No gravity. The geoid is a gravity-free surface of equal atmospheric pressure
Constant height. The geoid lies at a fixed elevation above the reference ellipsoid
Spherical. A perfect sphere centred on the Earth's centre of mass, unaffected by density
solution: Geoid: sea level if ocean at rest. Positive geoid = dense material below. Negative = less dense.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Electrical resistivity of rocks decreases with:
options: Increasing water saturation
Increasing dry rock density
Decreasing porosity and water
Increasing quartz content
solution: Resistivity: water-saturated rocks conduct better. Archie equation: R = Rw/φ^m × Sw^-n. More water = lower R.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the fine-grained volcanic rock that is the equivalent of granite?
options: Fine-grained equivalent of granite
Medium-grained andesite with plagioclase and hornblende phenocrysts
Natural volcanic glass lacking any crystalline structure
Coarse-grained basalt with olivine, pyroxene and calcic plagioclase
solution: Rhyolite: volcanic felsic. May contain glass (obsidian) or vesicles (pumice).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How is plagioclase feldspar classified on the basis of its anorthite (An) content?
options: The anorthite content is expressed as a single number for all plagioclase minerals because the composition never varies from pure albite
An content: An0-10 albite, An10-30 oligoclase, An30-50 andesine, An50-70 labradorite, An70-90 bytownite, An90-100 anorthite
An content from An0-100 is identical for all plagioclase minerals
Only two members exist with a discontinuous gap near An50
solution: Continuous solid solution. NaAlSi3O8 (albite) to CaAl2Si2O8 (anorthite).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Basalt is best classified as which kind of igneous rock based on its texture and composition?
options: Coarse-grained intrusive rock rich in quartz and alkali feldspar
Chemical sedimentary rock precipitated from a saturated brine solution
Fine-grained extrusive mafic igneous rock
High-grade metamorphic rock showing distinct compositional banding
solution: Basalt is the fine-grained, dark, mafic rock formed from rapidly cooled lava.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Foraminiferal tests are classified into which three wall types?
options: Aglutinated (cemented particles), Porous (calcareous), Imperforate (calcareous, non-porous)
All tests are siliceous. Opaline spicules cement into a rigid, chambered framework
Only organic (chitinous) tests. Calcareous and agglutinated wall types never occur in foraminifera
Siliceous, with aragonitic forms restricted to deep-water agglutinated taxa
solution: Forams: test types. Planktonic: globigerina (Cretaceous-Recent). Benthic: benthic forams.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The magnetotelluric (MT) method uses what natural source field, and which parameter is measured from it?
options: Controlled dc current injected to map resistivity at shallow depth
Seismic waves generated by an airgun source to image deep crustal reflectors
Gravity measurements reduced for terrain to model the Moho depth beneath a basin
Natural EM field (lightning, solar wind). Measures impedance Z = E/H
solution: MT: deep crustal imaging. Low frequency → deep. Resistivity model. MTZ: mid-crustal conductor.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Chloritoid, an Fe-Mn-Al silicate with characteristic otter-shaped twins, forms under which metamorphic grade?
options: Mg-Al silicate with sector twinning in low-pressure contact rocks
High-grade mineral stable only in granulite facies rocks
Fe-Mn-Al silicate. Otter-shaped twins. Low-grade metamorphic
Na-Ca amphibole diagnostic of blueschist facies terrains
solution: Chloritoid: in low-medium grade metapelites. Ottrelite: Mn-rich variety.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which sedimentary structure sequence characterizes a deep sea turbidite facies?
options: Bouma sequence: Ta (massive), Tb (laminated), Tc (ripple), Td (parallel), Te (pelagic)
Bouma sequence reversed, with Te at the base and Ta at the top of each bed
Turbidites show inverse grading throughout and lack any Bouma divisions
Bouma sequence beginning with ripple lamination and ending with massive graded divisions
solution: Bouma: graded bed (Ta) → pelagic (Te). Submarine fan. Thick-bedded near channel axis.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How does the Dunham classification distinguish mudstone, wackestone, packstone, and grainstone?
options: Wentworth's grain-size scale applied to carbonate grains, silt and mud fractions only
Udden's phi-based scale adapted to classify carbonate mud and sand fractions
Folk classification based on allochems (grains) and orthochems (matrix or cement), distinguishing sparry, micritic and mixed cement types
Mudstone (<10% grains), Wackestone (>10% grains mud-supported), Packstone (grain-supported muddy), Grainstone (grain-supported mud-free)
solution: Dunham: based on depositional texture. Binds tone, framestone, rudstone, floatstone added.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What distinguishes braided from meandering fluvial depositional systems in sediment and gradient?
options: Only deep marine fans fed by turbidity currents on the continental slope
Only braided alluvial fans with debris flows at mountain fronts in arid regions
Braided (coarse, high gradient) and meandering (fine, low gradient)
Deltaic systems at river mouths prograding into marine basins with prodelta muds
solution: Braided: gravel bars. Meandering: point bars, floodplains. Both in alluvial settings.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which subdivisions (topset, foreset, bottomset) characterize the delta facies?
options: Only horizontal aggradation of a uniform sand sheet with no distinct sub-environments
Topset (plain), foreset (front), bottomset (prodelta). Gilbert-type ~30° foresets
Vertical aggradation alone, with no progradation or distinct topset-foreset structure
Only tidal channel deposits with bipolar cross-bedding and mud drapes present
solution: Gilbert delta: coarse-grained. River-dominated (birdfoot, Mississippi). Tide/wave-modified deltas.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How do submarine fan channels differ from lobes in terms of erosion and sediment stacking?
options: Lobes: erosional, deeply confined. Channels: depositional, unconfined and compensational in stacking
Channels and lobes have identical geometries and both erode the basin floor
Channels: depositional, aggradational. Lobes: erosional with levees and spillover
Channels: erosional, confined. Lobes: depositional, unconfined, compensational stacking
solution: Channels: bypass conduits. Lobes: depocenters. Compensation stacking: lobes fill topographic lows.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which description best fits the mineral chlorite, a common product of low-grade metamorphism?
options: Green, platy, low-grade metamorphic mineral. Mg-Fe-Al sheet silicate
Red, equant mineral that is typical of very high-grade granulite facies rocks
Colorless prismatic mineral that is stable only in blueschist facies
Anhydrous framework silicate that is characteristic of the eclogite facies
solution: Chlorite: common in greenschist facies. Prograde: chlorite → biotite at higher grade.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Seismic refraction first arrival interpretation: crossover distance:
options: Offset at which the head wave disappears and only reflection remains
Maximum distance over which the direct wave is recorded before decay
Spacing beyond which the direct wave arrives ahead of the head wave
Distance where refracted wave overtakes direct wave arrival
solution: Crossover: x_c = 2h√((V₂+V₁)/(V₂-V₁)). h = thickness of first layer.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Ore reserve classification: measured, indicated, inferred:
options: All three categories carry the same geological confidence and data density
No classification is used, as tonnage is always reported as a single figure
Measured resources carry the lowest geological confidence and the widest drill hole spacing of all three categories
Measured: highest confidence. Indicated: reasonable confidence. Inferred: lowest confidence
solution: JORC, NI 43-101 codes. Measured: close spacing. Indicated: wider spacing. Inferred: limited data.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A mineral has passed through 2 half-lives of an isotope whose half-life is 4.5 (in the given time units). Its age is:
solution: Age = number of half-lives × half-life = 2×4.5 = 9.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: On a structure contour map, what do lines of equal elevation represent on a geological surface such as bedding or a fault?
options: Lines of equal temperature on a buried geological surface within the subsurface
Lines of equal elevation on a geological surface (bedding, fault)
A map of topographic relief showing elevation contours of the ground surface
Lines connecting equal dip values measured on the surface of a fault plane
solution: Structure contours: V-shaped across valleys (opposite rule for dipping beds).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 4% moisture, 20% volatile matter and 10% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (4+20+10) = 66%.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In a groundwater flow net, flow lines are orthogonal to equipotential lines, and the seepage discharge is given by:
options: Flow lines that run exactly parallel to the equipotential lines of the groundwater flow field
The random pattern of groundwater movement that occurs through a heterogeneous aquifer body
Flow lines orthogonal to equipotential lines. Q = KH·(N_f/N_d). Used for seepage
A set of equipotential lines with no fixed relationship to the pattern of the flow lines
solution: Flow net: squares (curvilinear). N_f = flow channels. N_d = head drops. For dams, excavations.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The aluminium silicate mineral kyanite crystallizes in which crystal system?
options: Hexagonal
Orthorhombic
Monoclinic
Triclinic
solution: Kyanite (Al2SiO5) — BLUE, hardness 4.5-7 depending on direction. Highly anisotropic.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The width of a wave-cut platform is controlled primarily by the combined influence of which factors?
options: The width is controlled only by the rate of sea-level change
The width is controlled only by the rock resistance
The width is controlled only by the wave energy at the coast
Rate of sea-level change, rock resistance, wave energy
solution: Platform: wider in weak rock, high wave energy, stable sea level. Narrow: resistant rock, rapid sea-level change.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which interferometric SAR technique uses the phase difference between two radar images of an area to measure ground deformation?
options: Amplitude difference between the two SAR images, which is used for land cover classification
A colour composite of the visible and near-infrared optical wavelength bands of the image
Edge detection of the linear features that are present in an optical satellite scene
Phase difference between two SAR images → ground deformation (mm precision)
solution: InSAR: surface displacement. Subsidence, earthquakes, volcanoes. PS-InSAR for time series.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Under what conditions does soil liquefaction typically occur?
options: Dense cemented bedrock loses all of its strength when shaken by a large quake
Saturated loose sand → loses strength during shaking. Water table rise
Only saturated clay deposits undergo liquefaction during shaking
Loose dry sand gains strength during strong earthquake shaking
solution: Liquefaction: Sand boils, lateral spreading, settlement. SPT-based triggering assessment.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which intergrowth texture shows quartz rods in feldspar, resembling cuneiform writing?
options: Porphyritic fabric with large phenocrysts set in a fine-grained groundmass
Trachytic alignment of plagioclase microlites recording lava flow direction
Granophyric intergrowth of quartz and alkali feldspar in granitic rocks
Quartz rods in feldspar — intergrowth. Like cuneiform writing
solution: Graphic: quartz-feldspar intergrowth. Simultaneous crystallization of eutectic-like melt.
